name: Local WordPress.org
description: WordPress.org is the open-source publishing platform that site owners install on infrastructure they control. Local WordPress installations support posts, pages, drafts, themes, plugins, media, users, configuration, and extensibility without requiring a WordPress.com account.
agentUseSummary: Bind one exact WordPress installation path on one trusted source host, then let selected agents read bounded site and post metadata or create one draft through the official WP-CLI under Safe or Dangerously skip permissions. Railway remains Relay's backend source of truth while WordPress content executes only on the bound source host.

credentialRequirements.name: LOCAL_WORDPRESS_ORG_SOURCE_HOST_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Source host
credentialRequirements.helpText: A connected Hermes or OpenClaw source host with WP-CLI and the intended local WordPress.org installation.

credentialRequirements.name: LOCAL_WORDPRESS_ORG_SOURCE_HOST_TYPE
credentialRequirements.label: Source host type
credentialRequirements.helpText: The exact hermes_bridge, openclaw_bridge, or runtime_host authority.

credentialRequirements.name: LOCAL_WORDPRESS_ORG_SITE_PATH
credentialRequirements.label: WordPress installation path
credentialRequirements.helpText: One exact absolute path containing the intended wp-config.php. Relay stores it encrypted, hashes it in audits, and never exposes it to agents.

capabilities.label: Read local site
capabilities.description: Read the home URL, list at most twenty post or page metadata records, and read one exact post or page with bounded content.

capabilities.label: Create local drafts
capabilities.description: Create one bounded post or page forced to draft with comments and pings closed.

approvalRequired.label: Read site identity
approvalRequired.description: Read the home URL for one exact local WordPress installation.

approvalRequired.label: List posts or pages
approvalRequired.description: List at most twenty bounded post or page metadata records for one explicit status.

approvalRequired.label: Read post or page
approvalRequired.description: Read one exact post or page with bounded editor content.

approvalRequired.label: Create draft
approvalRequired.description: Create one post or page forced to draft with comments and pings closed.

blocked.label: Publish or schedule content
blocked.description: Publishing, scheduling and changing the status of existing content are unavailable.

blocked.label: Update or delete existing content
blocked.description: Existing posts, pages, media, comments, terms and metadata cannot be changed, trashed or deleted.

blocked.label: Administer WordPress
blocked.description: Users, roles, passwords, options, plugins, themes, core, databases, cache, cron, multisite, menus, widgets, imports, exports and server administration are unavailable.

blocked.label: Run raw WP-CLI commands
blocked.description: Agents cannot supply executable names, global flags, command names, arbitrary query arguments, PHP, shell commands or filesystem paths.

blocked.label: Expose the local site remotely
blocked.description: Relay does not start a server, open a tunnel, add an application password, expose loopback traffic or redirect the web app from Railway.

blocked.label: Transfer unbounded content
blocked.description: Lists are capped at twenty, one exact post read is capped at 64 KiB, and draft content is capped at 16 KiB.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Private local site reads and draft creation require approval. Exact source-host and site-path binding, fixed WP-CLI commands, response bounds and audits always apply.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: All four selected operations run without Relay per-action approval; exact source-host and site-path binding, fixed WP-CLI commands, draft-only writes, response bounds and audits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway registers bounded tools and dispatches only to the exact connected OpenClaw source host and WordPress installation path; no remote WordPress API is opened.
Railway registers bounded tools and dispatches only to the exact connected Hermes source host and WordPress installation path; no remote WordPress API is opened.

providerSetup.nextAction: The customer installs the current official WP-CLI on a dedicated trusted source host, uses a least-privilege operating-system account, verifies the exact local WordPress.org installation path and backup, and connects that source host. WP-CLI boots WordPress PHP; --skip-plugins and --skip-themes reduce but do not eliminate site-code execution because must-use plugins can still load.

evidence.supports: WordPress.org identifies WP-CLI as the command-line interface for WordPress and documents scriptable administration of posts, core, plugins, databases and other site functions.
The official command reference documents post listing with post type, status, query arguments, selected fields, ordering and JSON output. Relay fixes and bounds those arguments.
The official command reference documents reading one exact post with selected fields and JSON output.
The official command reference documents creating a post and returning its ID; Relay fixes status to draft and closes comments and pings.
WordPress separately documents a remote REST API. This provider intentionally does not enable or expose that transport and is distinct from WordPress.com.
WordPress.org documents WordPress as free software released under the GPL, supporting customer-controlled local installation rather than a provider-hosted account flow.
